title: Sinners chosen to show the healing of souls
source_text: Ἐπεὶ δὲ καὶ ἐπιῤῥήτους εἶπεν ἀνθρώπους, τελώνας καὶ ναύτας πονηροτάτους λέγων ὁ Κέλσος τοὺς ἀποστόλους Ἰησοῦ, καὶ περὶ τούτου φήσομεν ὅτι ἔοικεν, ἵνα μὲν ἐγκαλέσῃ τῷ λόγῳ, πιστεύειν ὅπου θέλει τοῖς γεγραμμένοις. ἵνα δὲ τὴν ἐμφαινομένην θειότητα ἐν τοῖς αὐτοῖς βιβλίοις ἀπαγγελλομένην μὴ παραδέξηται, ἀπιστεῖν τοῖς εὐαγγελίοις· δέον τὸ φιλάληθες ἰδόντα τῶν γραψάντων ἐκ τῆς περὶ τῶν χειρόνων ἀναγραφῆς πιστεῦσαι καὶ περὶ τῶν θειοτέρων. γέγραπται δὴ ἐν τῇ Βαρνάβα καθολικῇ ἐπιστολῇ, ὅθεν ὁ Κέλσος λαβὼν τάχα εἶπεν εἶναι ἐπιῤῥήτους καὶ πονηροτάτους τοὺς ἀποστόλους, ὅτι „ἐξελέξατο τοὺς ἰδίους ἀποστόλους“ Ἰησοῦς, „ὄντας ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν ἀνομίαν ἀνομωτέρους.“ καὶ ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ δὲ τῷ κατὰ Αουκᾶν φησι πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὁ Πέτρος· „ἔξελθε ἀπ᾿ ἐμοῦ, ὅτι ἀνὴρ ἁμαρτωλός εἰμι, κύριε.“ ἀλλὰ καὶ ὁ Παῦλος ἐν τῇ πρὸς Τιμόθεόν φησι, καὶ αὐτὸς ὕστερον ἀπόστολος Ἰησοῦ γενόμενος, ὅτι „πιστὸς ὁ λόγος,“ „ὅτι Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἦλθεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἁμαρτωλοὺς σῶσαι, ὧν πρῶτός εἰμι ἐγώ.“ οὐκ οἶδα δ᾿ ὅπως ἐπελάθετο ἢ οὐκ ἐνόησεν περὶ Παύλου τι εἰπεῖν, τοῦ μετὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν τὰς ἐν Χριστῷ πήξαντος ἐκκλησίας. εἰκὸς γὰρ ὅτι ἑώρα δεῖσθαι αὐτῷ ἀπολογίας τὸν περὶ Παύλου λόγον, πῶς διώξας τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ πικρῶς ἀγωνισάμενος κατὰ τῶν πιστευόντων, ὡς καὶ εἰς θάνατον παραδιδόναι ἐθέλειν τοὺς Ἰησοῦ μαθητὰς, ὕστερον ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον μετεβάλετο, ὡς „ἀπὸ Ἱερουσαλὴμ μέχρι τοῦ Ἰλλυρικοῦ πεπληρωκέναι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ“ καὶ „φιλοτιμούμενον εὐαγγελίζεσθαι,“ ὥστε „μὴ ἐπ᾿ ἀλλότριον θεμέλιον“ οἰκοδομεῖν, ἀλλ᾿ ὅπου μηδὲ τὴν ἀρχὴν ἐκηρύχθη τὸ ἐν Χριστῷ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ θεοῦ. τί οὖν ἄτοπον βουλόμενον παραστῆσαι τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὸν Ἰησοῦν, ὁπηλίκην ἔχει ψυχῶν ἰατρικὴν, τοὺς ἐπιῤῥήτους καὶ πονηροτάτους ἐπιλέξασθαι καὶ τούτους προαγαγεῖν ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον, ὥστ᾿ αὐτοὺς παράδειγμα εἶναι ἤθους καθαρωτάτου τοῖς δι᾿ αὐτῶν προσαγομένοις τῷ Χριστοῦ εὐαγγελίῳ;
pass_a_gloss: Since Celsus also called the apostles of Jesus notorious (ἐπιρρήτους) men, saying tax collectors and sailors most wicked, about this too we will say that he seems (ἔοικεν), in order to accuse (ἐγκαλέσῃ) the word/teaching (τῷ λόγῳ), to believe the writings (γεγραμμένοις) where he wishes, but, in order not to accept (παραδέξηται) the divinity (θειότητα) appearing proclaimed in the same books, to disbelieve (ἀπιστεῖν) the Gospels; it being necessary (δέον), having seen the truth-loving (τὸ φιλάληθες) of the writers from the recording (ἀναγραφῆς) of the worse things (χειρόνων), to believe also about the more divine (θειοτέρων). It is written then in the catholic epistle (καθολικῇ ἐπιστολῇ) of Barnabas, whence Celsus taking perhaps said the apostles were notorious and most wicked, that Jesus 'chose his own apostles, being more lawless (ἀνομωτέρους) beyond all lawlessness (ἀνομίαν)'. And in the Gospel according to Luke Peter says to Jesus: 'go out from me, for I am a sinful (ἁμαρτωλός) man, Lord.' But also Paul in the [letter] to Timothy says, himself too later having become an apostle of Jesus, that 'faithful (πιστός) the word', 'that Jesus Christ came into the world to save sinners, of whom first am I'. I do not know how he forgot or did not think to say something about Paul, who after Jesus fixed/established (πήξαντος) the churches in Christ. For likely (εἰκός) he saw that the account (λόγον) about Paul needed a defence (ἀπολογίας) by him: how, having persecuted (διώξας) the church of God and having struggled bitterly (πικρῶς) against the believers, so as to wish even to hand over to death the disciples of Jesus, later he changed (μετεβάλετο) so much as 'from Jerusalem to Illyricum to have fulfilled (πεπληρωκέναι) the gospel of Christ' and 'being ambitious (φιλοτιμούμενον) to evangelize', so as 'not on another's foundation (ἀλλότριον θεμέλιον)' to build, but where not even at all (τὴν ἀρχήν) the gospel of God in Christ was preached. What then is absurd (ἄτοπον), Jesus wishing to present to the race of men how great a healing art (ἰατρικήν) of souls he has, to choose the notorious and most wicked and to lead them forward (προαγαγεῖν) so far that they are an example (παράδειγμα) of purest character (ἤθους καθαρωτάτου) to those brought (προσαγομένοις) through them to the gospel of Christ?
pass_b_english: Since Celsus also called the apostles of Jesus notorious men, saying that they were “tax collectors and sailors of the worst sort,” we will say about this too that he seems to believe what is written where he wishes, so that he can bring a charge against our teaching, but to disbelieve the Gospels so that he need not accept the Godhead plainly proclaimed in those same books. Yet he ought to have recognised the writers' love of truth from their record of the less creditable things, and so to have believed them about the more divine things too.

Now it is written in the catholic epistle of Barnabas, from which Celsus perhaps took his claim that the apostles were notorious and of the worst sort, that Jesus “chose his own apostles, who were more lawless than all lawlessness” (Epistle of Barnabas 5:9). And in the Gospel according to Luke, Peter says to Jesus: “Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord” (Luke 5:8). Paul too, who himself afterwards became an apostle of Jesus, says in the letter to Timothy: “The saying is trustworthy, that Jesus Christ came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the first” (1 Timothy 1:15).

I do not know how Celsus forgot, or did not think, to say something about Paul, who after Jesus firmly founded the churches that are in Christ. For it is likely that he saw that the story of Paul would call for an answer from him: how Paul, after he had persecuted the church of God (Galatians 1:13) and fought bitterly against the believers, so far as to want to hand the disciples of Jesus over to death (Acts 22:4), later changed so greatly that “from Jerusalem as far as Illyricum” he “fully preached the gospel of Christ” (Romans 15:19), “making it his aim to preach the gospel” so as not to build “on someone else's foundation” (Romans 15:20), but to build where the gospel of God in Christ had not been preached at all.

What is out of place, then, if Jesus, wishing to show the human race how great a skill in healing souls he has, chose men who were notorious and of the worst sort, and led them on so far that they became a pattern of the purest character for those who were brought through them to the gospel of Christ?

choices.choice: 'Tax collectors and sailors of the worst sort' repeats Celsus's words from 1.62 and is kept in quotation marks. τῷ λόγῳ ('our teaching') is the Christian message, as often in this work. The staged text has Αουκᾶν (read Λουκᾶν, Luke) and ἁνθρώπων with a stray rough breathing (read ἀνθρώπων). The Epistle of Barnabas, which Origen calls 'catholic', is quoted from 5:9 (ὄντας ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν ἁμαρτίαν ἀνομωτέρους in the received text of Barnabas; Origen's copy has ἀνομίαν, 'lawlessness', which is translated); it is not canonical Scripture and is cited inline by its own name, not listed in bible_refs. Luke 5:8 is quoted exactly. 1 Timothy 1:15 is quoted with the order Ἰησοῦς Χριστός ('Jesus Christ'), where many New Testament witnesses read 'Christ Jesus'; Origen's order is kept. 'Persecuted the church of God' echoes Galatians 1:13 and 1 Corinthians 15:9 (both have τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ θεοῦ); Galatians 1:13 is cited inline. The wish to hand disciples over to death is a clear allusion to Acts 22:4 (compare Acts 9:1 and 26:10). Romans 15:19 is quoted without κύκλῳ ('round about'), so the English has 'as far as Illyricum'; Romans 15:20 is quoted in part, and the closing clause ('where the gospel ... had not been preached at all') is Origen's paraphrase of Paul's 'not where Christ had been named'. ἀπολογία is rendered 'call for an answer': Celsus would have had to account for Paul's conversion.
'the Godhead that is shown to be proclaimed' (stiff) changed to 'the Godhead plainly proclaimed' for ἐμφαινομένην ... ἀπαγγελλομένην
δέον ... ἰδόντα: 'when he saw ... he ought to have believed' asserted that Celsus saw; changed to 'he ought to have recognised ... and so to have believed'
restored γάρ ('For it is likely'); ἀπολογίας: 'explaining away' (interpretive) changed to 'call for an answer from him'; note updated
Romans 15:20: 'another man's' changed to 'someone else's' (ἀλλότριον); elliptical 'but where' completed as 'but to build where' from οἰκοδομεῖν
ἰατρικήν: 'power to heal souls' changed to 'skill in healing souls'; προαγαγεῖν: 'led them on'
checked Barnabas 5:9, Luke 5:8, 1 Timothy 1:15, Galatians 1:13, Acts 22:4, Romans 15:19–20 against the quoted words
